title: Illumina SpliceAI Deep Dilated CNN Uncovers Cryptic RNA Splicing Mutations Driving Autism and Intellectual Disability
whyItMatters: Published in Cell, SpliceAI’s 32-layer dilated CNN predicted cryptic RNA splicing from 10-kb DNA windows—uncovering hidden pathogenic mutations accounting for ~10% of genetic diagnoses in autism and intellectual disability.
summary: Published in Cell on January 17, 2019, Kishore Jaganathan, Sofia Kyriazopoulou Panagiotopoulou, Jeremy F. McRae, Kyle Kai-How Farh, and collaborators at Illumina Artificial Intelligence Laboratory introduced SpliceAI, a 32-layer deep residual dilated convolutional neural network scanning 10,000 nucleotides of raw pre-mRNA sequence context to predict splice donor and acceptor sites with 95% top-k accuracy. Applying SpliceAI to clinical cohorts of patients with autism spectrum disorder and severe intellectual disability uncovered previously missed de novo cryptic splicing mutations—experimentally validated by RNA-seq—accounting for roughly 9–11% of pathogenic genetic diagnoses in those cohorts and transforming clinical rare-disease diagnostics worldwide.
technicalHighlights: Expanded genomic CNN context to 10 kb via 32 dilated residual layers, achieving 95% top-k accuracy predicting exon-intron boundaries from primary sequence alone.
Discovered previously missed pathogenic de novo cryptic splicing mutations in autism and severe intellectual disability, confirmed by patient RNA-seq.
Became a clinical diagnostic standard worldwide for interpreting rare-disease whole-genome variants.
caveats: Predicts constitutive pre-mRNA splicing disruptions rather than full cell-type-specific alternative isoform abundance (later addressed by Pangolin and AlphaGenome).

scoreRationale.foundational: Solved long-range sequence-to-splicing prediction and directly discovered a major hidden class of pathogenic mutations in human neurodevelopmental disorders.
scoreRationale.ripple: Adopted globally in clinical rare-disease genome diagnostics and directly paved the way for AlphaMissense and AlphaGenome.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Cell (Vol. 176, pp. 535–548) with direct RNA-seq validation in patient cohorts and clinical replication.
scoreRationale.velocity: Screens entire patient genomes for cryptic splicing pathology in minutes.
